identification: Early 1900s blue and white vitreous enamel street name sign 'ELIZABETH ST' on steel, border lines, two fixing holes, chips and rust at corners and holes, rust patch over the S, rusty back, old inventory label S648/9. Small (about 60 cm long by 12 cm high judging from photos, size not confirmed). No maker or council mark seen. Elizabeth St is a common street name (Hobart, Launceston, Melbourne, Brisbane and others), so the town matters.

chrome_hint: 1) eBay AU sold + completed: 'enamel street sign', 'ELIZABETH ST enamel sign', 'vintage enamel street name sign' (Terapeak last 12 months, Australia, note size and condition). 2) Leski Auctions realised prices: 'street sign enamel'. 3) Gowans, Mossgreen/Theodore Bruce, Davidson Auctions, Burns & Co (bidsonline): 'enamel street sign' and 'Elizabeth St'. 4) LiveAuctioneers / Invaluable: 'enamel street sign Australia'. 5) Check whether Elizabeth St is a Hobart, Launceston or Melbourne sign (local streets sell better).
viewing_check: Measure the sign (length and height) and look for council or maker marks (e.g. Stewart & Co, Wunderlich, Hobart or Launceston Municipal) on the back or edge; check the rust over the S and chip extent at the holes; the S648/9 label is probably an old collection or dealer stock number. Any provenance as a Hobart or Launceston Elizabeth St sign would lift value.
